title: FLORA HYDRANT FLUSHING
full_story:
The City of Flora Water Department will be doing hydrant flushing today and tomorrow from 7:30 am until approximately 3:30 pm each day.

Although it may appear to be a waste of water, the process is part of a routine maintenance program necessary to maintain the integrity of the water system, allowing the city to continue to deliver the highest quality water possible to customers.  As a result of the line flushing process, residents in the immediate vicinity of the work may experience temporary discoloration of their water.  This discoloration consists primarily of harmless silt and air and does not affect the safety of the water.

If you experience discoloration in your water after crews have been flushing in your neighborhood, clear the pipes in your home by running all water faucets for a few minutes.  Washing light colored laundry is not recommended during this period.  The same philosophy of water line preventive maintenance is one that you should use in your own home to ensure the quality of water inside your home.  Your home’s water heater should be drained and flushed on a regular basis, according to manufacturers’ recommendations, to keep it working effectively and efficiently.

title: CLAY ELECTRIC COOP SCHOLARSHIPS
full_story:
Clay Electric Cooperative will be drawing for three $500 scholarships for the children of its members at its 82nd Annual Meeting to be held tomorrow night.

All registered member in attendance will get $15 off their next bill.  Members will enjoy a pork chop or chicken dinner, live entertainment featuring Guy Ash, and learn about the cooperative and the business meeting at 6:30 pm.  Those who attend will also be entered into a drawing for more bill credits or the grand prize Ninja cooler.

Scholarships will be drawn live at the end of the meeting which will be held at the Oilbelt Christian Service Camp on tomorrow night starting at 5 pm.

title: FORD TOWN FUN FEST 2026
full_story:
Ford Town Fun Fest is Friday, September 18th and Saturday, September 19th.

The location for the festival is in front of the Flora Public Library and Food trucks will be set up on East 2nd Street.

The event starts with a Cruise in Friday from 5 pm, starting at the parking lot of Beck’s Auto Sales with dash plaques to the first 100 entries.  The car show is open to any make or model of car.  They will be cruising through town and past Heritage Woods so the residents can look at the vehicles.  Food trucks inflatables and family yard games will be available at Library Park from 5 to 8 pm, and Just for Spite Unplugged will be playing from 6 to 9 pm.

Saturday the Clay County Cruisers will have a Car Show with registration from 9 until Noon.  The car show registration is $15 and there will be awards for the top 75 plus 5 specialty awards.  For Car show information call 618-676-4005, 618-662-5646 or 618-676-7732.  Dash plaques will be given to the first 100 entrants.  Craft and food vendors, inflatables, and games will also open at 9 am.  There are also commemorative t-shirts available for $20.

At noon the craft brew and chili cookoff sampling will begin and the dunking booth will open.  Car show awards are at 3 pm and craft beer and chili judging will begin at 4 pm.  So far there are 7 entries in the craft brew contest and 6 entries in the Chili Cookoff, with entries still being taken.  The winner of the Chili Cookoff will win a $100 gift card and have their name engraved on the Chili Cookoff Plaque in City Hall.  For more information call Arriel at the Chamber Office at 618-662-5646.

Arriel Dulaney and Stephen Smith are todays guests on the ReVue to talk about upcoming Chamber events and Ford Town.

title: FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY FALL BOOK SALE
full_story:
The Friends of the Flora Public Library Fall Book Sale will be held on Saturday, September 12th from 8 am to 3 pm and the library is seeking donations.

Anyone wishing to contribute to the book sale can bring books that are in good shape to the front desk.  The library is also accepting CD’s DVD’s and magazines.  The Flora Public Library is open Monday through Thursday 1:00 – 8:00 pm, Friday 10:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday 10:00 am to 3:00 pm.  The library has a handcart to assist individuals who may be bringing a large volume of materials in.

The day of the sale all books, DVD’s and CD’s will be .25 cents.  Magazines are 10 cents each or 12 for $1.

title: LAKE SHELBYVILLE DEER STAND AUCTION
full_story:
Friends of Lake Shelbyville, an association that works with the US Army Corps of Engineers’, is holding a silent auction for impounded deer stands and climbing sticks on Saturday.  You’ll need to head to the government vehicle lot south of the Lake Shelbyville Visitor Center from 7:30 to 10:30 am.  Organizers say 25 tree stands will be up for bid, ranging from two-man ladder stands to single-man ladders and mobile hunting stands.

Proceeds from the auction go toward funding the Annual Youth Deer Hunt in October and the Annual Disabled Deer Hunt in November, so every bid helps support those programs.  Anyone interested can view all the stands and sticks in person that morning before deciding what to bid on.

Bidders will need to fill out a bid sheet with their contact information, the stand numbers they’re bidding on, and their bid amounts, along with a liability form releasing the Army Corps of Engineers from responsibility if an accident were to occur following your purchase.  Sealed bids will be opened at 10:30 am, and stands will be awarded to the high bidders at 11 am that same morning.  If a high bidder isn’t present at that time, the stand goes to the next highest bidder, and stands cannot be held or picked up later.

Any questions about the silent auction or Lake Shelbyville’s Tree Stand Policy can contact Park Ranger Tanner Coleman at 217-774-3951, ext. 7006, or visit the Lake Shelbyville website for more information.

title: WORKING GROUP LOSES ANOTHER
full_story:
At the Illinois State Fair last week, controversy surrounding ethics, transparency and complaints against lawmakers followed politicians from the State Capitol to the state fairgrounds just 3 miles north.

A “workplace culture and accountability” working group was created by House Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch in response to issues of sexual harassment by former member Representative Harry Benton.

Following the investigation and resignation of Benton this summer, Welch faced scrutiny both from his caucus and across the aisle over his handling of early complaints of sexual harassment by Benton, and his financial support for Benton’s previous reelection campaign thereafter.

A third member, state Representative Tracy Katz Muhl, has publicly withdrawn from participating in the group.

House Minority Leader Tony McCombie at a Republican Day event at the State Fair on Thursday was critical of the working group and said the House Dems should have a third party handling internal complaints, rather than self-policing.

“Even the governor has concerns with this work group.  You don’t need to have a working group to take some of our ethics bills that are already out there,” McCombie said.  “We don’t need any sort of working group to have HR.  We have HR that can do in-house, you know, under the dome and out in the district.  So do the Senate Dems.”

McCombie’s comments come as Governor Pritzker said a day before that Welch admitted the process of investigating Benton was “inadequate.”

Pritzker was questioned on his financial support of House Democrat candidates close to Welch.

“I support Democrats up and down the ballot, and have supported individual candidates for my entire, not just time in office, but for probably my entire adult life.  So, I’m going to continue to do that,” Pritzker said on Wednesday.

Pritzker previously said the working group needed to work quickly, though no details have been made public on if the group has met or begun working on recommendations to reform the process of making internal complaints against lawmakers.

Welch’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment from The Center Square.

McCombie was also critical of Welch for his “unwritten rule of 60,” where he requires a minimum of 60 House Dems to support a piece of legislation before it is called in the chamber; effectively blocking bills that may have bipartisan support, but not enough Democrats on board.

“We’re the only caucus that represents all of the 102 counties.  We have a variety of different education, job experience, life experience.  We should be included in those conversations.  But the Speaker continues with his unwritten rule of 60,” McCombie said.

title: TORNADO RECORD
full_story:
Illinois State Climatologist Trent Ford continues to add up tornadoes in 2026, and the numbers keep climbing.

Fifteen have occurred in August, pushing the state to over the 200-number mark, which shatters the previous record of 142 set in 2024.

Ford is in the process of putting together a 2026 timeline.  “Some of these have been so long ago that it feels like we forgot about them,” he said.

The first tornado outbreak occurred in mid-February.  “We had 14 tornadoes strewn across southeast Illinois from Effingham County over to the Indiana border,” Ford said.

Multiple tornado outbreaks also happened in March.  “There was one along the I70 corridor from the St. Louis Metro East area up to the Effingham area,” he said.  “We also had those really intense storms that moved across from LaSalle to Kankakee, so we had about 30 tornadoes in March.”

April was a very active month with 70 tornadoes impacting the state.  “Most of those were in central Illinois, including a lot in Logan County and Tazewell County,” Ford said.  “There was an EF2 tornado in Lena, which was an intense event in April.”

May was a quiet month with just one tornado, but things ramped back up in June with 90 tornadoes across the state.  “Again hot spots were in central and southeast Illinois, including an EF3 that spun up north of Peoria and the Washburn area and moved across and caused some damage in Dwight and Streator,” he said.

July included 10 tornadoes with several in the Chicagoland area; 15 tornadoes have been recorded this month with most in northern Illinois.

title: STELLANTIS RECALL
full_story:
Automaker Stellantis said Monday that it is recalling nearly 850,000 vehicles in the US over a software issue that can disrupt the rearview camera display.

The affected vehicles include Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep and Ram vehicles with model years ranging from 2026 to 2027.  Stellantis said it is unaware of any accidents or injuries related to the software glitch.

The car manufacturer is also recalling another 107,000 vehicles in Canada, Mexico and other markets outside of North America over the same issue, according to the company’s notice.

Recalled vehicles in the US include: 2026-27 Chrysler Pacifica, Pacifica Plug-in Hybrid and Voyager minivans, 2026-27 Dodge Charger vehicles, 2026 Jeep Cherokee, Compass, Gladiator, Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer L and Wrangler vehicles and 2026 Ram 1500 and 2500 pickups and ProMaster and ProMaster EV vans.

Owners of affected vehicles in the US will receive an over-the-air radio software update, Stellantis said Monday.

If the rearview display is not working, the company said drivers “should remain aware of their surroundings and use their rearview and side mirrors when reversing.”
